summary: Berk's is a family-run 3PL/public warehouse founded in 1982, headquartered at 4000 Bordentown Avenue in Sayreville, NJ, that has grown from a single 3,000 sq ft facility to a claimed 2,000,000 sq ft across seven sites (Sayreville NJ, Allentown PA, Mt Pocono PA, Norfolk VA, Pooler GA, Dallas TX, Colton CA). It serves apparel, textile/hospitality, consumer electronics, perfume, toy and appliance shippers with carton and pallet handling, pick-and-pack, e-commerce/VDC fulfillment, cross-dock and value-added work such as ticketing, QC, SKU/UPC verification and EDI processing. Intake appears entirely phone-and-form based with no published hours, careers page, booking tool or customer-facing content, while second-generation leadership took on customer onboarding, business development and IT in 2020.

facts.fact: Founded in 1982; company states it started with 3,000 sq ft and has grown to over 2,000,000 sq ft.
Facilities listed as Sayreville NJ (headquarters), Allentown PA, Mt Pocono PA, Norfolk VA, Pooler GA, Dallas TX and Colton CA.
Headquarters address is 4000 Bordentown Avenue, Sayreville, NJ 08872, described as 26 miles from the Port of Newark/Elizabeth and just off the Garden State Parkway.
Service lines: carton in/carton out, carton in/piece out (pick and pack), e-commerce, pallet in/pallet out (cross-dock) and value-added services.
Value-added work includes ticketing/marking/bundling, QC inspections, SKU/UPC verification and application, hanger/polybag work, EDI processing and pick ticket/invoice/UCC label printing.

E-commerce/VDC fulfillment uses in-house proprietary software that scans each piece and prints packing lists and labels; orders are received by file upload, third-party integration (Commerce Hub, SPS Commerce, B2B Gateway) or retailer portals, with most orders processed within 24 hours.
Client verticals listed: fashion & apparel, textiles/hospitality, consumer electronics, perfume, toys, household appliances.

Principals Michael Gross and Jack Berkowitz each have 30+ years of experience and work on the warehouse floor; Matthew Gross joined in 2020 and handles customer onboarding, business development and the IT department.

Contact page lists the business as Berk's Warehousing & Transportation at the Sayreville address with phone (732) 254-9955 and the instruction 'Ask for Michael or Matthew'; the site header separately shows (732) 254-4777, and the only web intake is a generic cforms contact form.
In the April 2025 archived homepage, the same paragraph states growth to 'over 750,000 square feet'; the live homepage now states 'over 2,000,000 square feet'.
The site is a WordPress install running version 3.8.10, and its sitemap shows page content last modified between 2012 and 2015 with no careers, news or blog pages.

operations_signals: No online quote, booking or scheduling tool anywhere on the site; the only digital intake is a generic cforms contact form that posts to the company with no routing, qualification or confirmation described (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/contact)

Two different phone numbers are published on the same contact page — (732) 254-4777 in the site header and (732) 254-9955 in the page body — plus the instruction to 'ask for Michael or Matthew', implying phone-based, named-person routing of inquiries (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/contact)
No business hours, holiday schedule, dock appointment process or after-hours/emergency coverage is published anywhere on the site; contact is 'call today' (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/contact)
Service area is a seven-site network spanning NJ, PA, VA, GA, TX and CA, all coordinated from the Sayreville headquarters (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/location/)

Order flow is document-heavy and channel-specific: file uploads, EDI/3rd-party integrations (Commerce Hub, SPS Commerce, B2B Gateway) and retailer-specific portals, each set up individually per client (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/ecommerce/)
Client-facing visibility is through the in-house WMS web access, which also exposes container availability information (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/about)

Shipping cadence is daily and time-boxed: UPS and FedEx make multiple pickups per day and major LTL carriers pick up daily, with most orders processed within 24 hours and expedited service offered (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/ecommerce/)

Customers are B2B shippers/retail vendors (brands supplying retailers and marketplaces), not consumers; the site lists retailer relationships including Bed Bath and Beyond.com, Overstock.com, Kohls.com, Costco.com and Amazon.com (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/ecommerce/)
hiring_signals: No careers, jobs or employment page exists on the site and no such page appears in the site's sitemap, so hiring appears to run entirely off-site (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/sitemap.xml)

Roles implied by the service mix rather than advertised: pick/pack and VAS floor labor, QC inspectors, EDI/document processing, inventory/cycle-count clerks, customer onboarding and IT support (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/carton-in-piece-out-pick-and-pack/)
Inference: no job-board evidence could be collected because every search provider and job board attempted (Indeed, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn) was blocked or rate-limited in this environment (no source)
review_themes: No public customer or employee reviews could be retrieved — Google, Yelp, BBB, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter and LinkedIn were blocked (403/429) or unreachable, and no search provider returned results (no source)
tech_footprint: Website is WordPress 3.8.10 (circa 2014) with a sitemap generated in 2015 and page content last touched in 2012–2015; no blog, news, resource or careers content (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/sitemap.xml)
Contact form is the 'cforms' plugin by delicious:days, an old lightweight form plugin with no CRM, chat or marketing-automation integration visible (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/contact)
No live chat, chatbot, booking widget, customer portal login, pricing tool or e-commerce checkout appears anywhere on the public site (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/)

Proprietary in-house WMS and order-processing programming (scans each piece, auto-prints packing list and label) with client web access and container availability data (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/ecommerce/)

Document/data integrations: Commerce Hub, SPS Commerce, B2B Gateway, retail portals, and EDI processing performed as a value-added service (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/services/value-added-services/)

Site copy is inconsistent between pages on a headline metric (750,000 vs 2,000,000 sq ft: the About page still shows the older 750,000 figure), suggesting light content-ops maintenance (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/about)
growth_signals: Footprint expanded from 3,000 sq ft at founding in 1982 to a claimed 2,000,000 sq ft across seven states (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/)

The square-footage claim on the homepage rose from 'over 750,000' in the April 2025 archived version to 'over 2,000,000' today — a step-change in claimed capacity within roughly the last 18 months (http://web.archive.org/web/20250416191010/http://www.berkswarehouse.com/)
Succession in motion: second-generation Matthew Gross joined in 2020 and took customer onboarding, business development and IT (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/about)
Multi-state network (NJ, PA, VA, GA, TX, CA) implies multi-site coordination, cross-facility inventory and reporting rather than a single-DC operation (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/location/)

Positioning deliberately contrasts with competitors' 'expect a miracle' / 'crisis-mode' staffing language, i.e. the company sells itself on advance scheduling and on-time, on-budget processing (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/)
Apparel/textile and e-commerce retail verticals create seasonal peak swings typical of fashion and holiday fulfillment (https://www.berkswarehouse.com/verticals/)
decision_maker: Michael Gross — principal (co-owner) alongside principal Jack Berkowitz, both listed on the company's own About page; Matthew Gross (joined 2020) handles customer onboarding, business development and IT — source: https://www.berkswarehouse.com/about

inferences.inference: Inbound sales and customer service are handled manually by named people over the phone, with no automated intake, qualification or response-time promise.
inferences.reasoning: The only published channels are two phone numbers and a generic cforms form, the contact page literally says 'Ask for Michael or Matthew', and there is no booking, chat or quote tool on the site.

inferences.inference: A large share of staff time goes to document/data reconciliation across retailer-specific formats rather than physical handling alone.
inferences.reasoning: The company advertises EDI processing, pick ticket/invoice/UCC label printing, SKU/UPC verification and per-client setups across Commerce Hub, SPS Commerce, B2B Gateway and retailer portals — all structured but individually configured, i.e. classic rule-based exception work.

inferences.inference: IT and process ownership sits with one second-generation leader, which caps internal build capacity and makes outside AI tooling attractive.
inferences.reasoning: The About page assigns customer onboarding, business development and the entire IT department to Matthew Gross, while the public website still runs WordPress 3.8.10 with 2012–2015 content — a sign IT bandwidth is spent on operations, not on modernizing front-of-house.

inferences.inference: Multi-site coordination is the most likely source of customer-facing friction as the network grows.
inferences.reasoning: Seven facilities in six states are all coordinated from Sayreville, and the homepage markets the company on advance staff scheduling and 'not working in crisis-mode' — the promise most at risk when site count grows faster than coordination tooling.

inferences.inference: Seasonal labor and scheduling strain is likely, given fashion/apparel and e-commerce retail clients.
inferences.reasoning: The vertical list is dominated by apparel, textiles, consumer electronics and toys, all of which peak around back-to-school and holiday, while the site emphasizes pre-scheduling staff to hit on-time targets.

inferences.inference: The company's claimed capacity figures are unreliable enough that a buyer should confirm them directly.
inferences.reasoning: The live homepage says 2,000,000 sq ft while the About page and the April 2025 homepage both say 750,000 sq ft for the same network description.

data_gaps: No public reviews retrieved — review and job platforms (Google, Yelp, BBB, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn, MapQuest) returned 403/429 or unreadable JS pages, so customer-voice themes are unknown.
No job postings found; the site has no careers page and job boards could not be accessed, so current hiring volume and role mix are unverified.

All web search providers failed in this environment (rate limits or missing API keys), so no news, press releases, association listings or local coverage of expansions, awards or new locations could be located beyond the company's own site and a Wayback snapshot.
Employee count, revenue, and number of customers are not published anywhere on the site; no third-party company profile was reachable.
Business hours, dock appointment policy, after-hours/emergency coverage and service-area radius are not stated on the site.
The Colton, CA facility appears in the current homepage and locations list but the About page (and older archived copy) omits California entirely, so its status is unconfirmed.
No CRM, TMS, chat or marketing-automation tools are visible publicly; ownership of the in-house WMS and EDI stack cannot be assessed from outside.
No named titles beyond 'principals' are published; the legal entity name (e.g., whether 'Berk's Warehousing & Transportation' is the registered entity) was not verifiable.
